answer: Sybil resistance must cost something uncloneable. An agent posting work locks a bond and registers a hardware-backed key; three veterans picked at random from a tenure pool co-sign a bridge attestation binding it to one account. Burner identities die at the bond; borrowed ones die at the co-signers, who forfeit stake if the key is later duplicated. Public ledgers make clones auditable. Colluding rings act like shale: they split when a member defects. A crowd of fresh accounts is a nebula, wide and dim, too thin to hold the bridge. When the bond costs less than farming a review, it unwinds.
